proposal:
## Disposition

Revise. CH-1 through CH-5 are accepted in substance. The revision preserves three defenses: it rejects an all-basis successor offender count, corrects the false shared-contributor claim, and rejects unsupported legal implications from the 3D/flat grouping. CH-4 is accepted only as a finding about the observed runtime path.

No round-one content is incorporated by blanket reference. The retained positions are limited to those named in `accepted_points`; this revision controls where it changes Decisions A-D, acceptance criteria, risks, or requested actions.

## Presentation dependency - metadata-only capability

RIGHTS-001 requires a future OP-INTERFACE capability that can present a selected artwork record as metadata-only. This is not a fifth owner decision, does not exist in the current product, and is not authorized for implementation here.

Metadata-only is a deliberate text presentation, not a blank frame, loading state, broken image, or error. It preserves title, artist, date where available, navigation and links, existing record actions, and a plain media-status explanation. It renders no artwork image, photograph, scan, Pigment cover, canvas, image-role equivalent, or image alt text.

A3 and B1 independently invoke this capability for selected records. Their record-scoped treatment takes precedence over C1 or C2 only for those records. C3 invokes the same capability globally for the 61 existing cover-backed records. A genuinely independent editorial cover may remain only when it is not substituting for the artwork and is visibly and accessibly labelled `Editorial cover - not the artwork`.

## Decision A - five named-media-author records

Decision A governs the five records whose source pages name a media author. For evidence review they remain grouped as three photographs of three-dimensional underlying works (`david`, `pieta`, `little-dancer-aged-fourteen`) and two photographs of flat underlying works (`black-fuji`, `vahine-no-te-tiare`). This is an analytical grouping, not a demonstrated legal distinction.

The current generated registry and census record source assertions naming Sailko and CC BY 3.0 for the exact `black-fuji` media file, and Francesco Bini and CC BY-SA 4.0 for the exact `vahine-no-te-tiare` media file. Pigment does not determine authorship, authority, separate protectable expression, or legal effect.

A1 retains a conditional-basis vocabulary for the five named-author records. A2 retains record-by-record re-sourcing. A3 withholds the five exact media assets and independently requires record-scoped metadata-only presentation from future OP-INTERFACE work; it does not select C3. A4 retains the current media and source-derived credits as a dated owner exception while the vocabulary defect and residual questions remain recorded.

If A1 is selected, the literal-token ratchet is retired only with future successor guards scoped to the five A1-migrated records. Those guards must preserve exact media identity, source page and revision, source-asserted author, licence family and version, and generated-credit continuity, and must be shown non-vacuous through recorded negative controls. The sixth record is included only if B separately changes it. These are future acceptance requirements, not claims that successor guards presently exist.

## Decision B - `the-ten-largest-no-9`

Decision B separately governs the unnamed or conflicted af Klint media asset and alternatives. The current source assertions remain attached to the exact media candidates and are not converted into a Pigment finding or source preference.

B1 applies record-scoped metadata-only presentation to this record and independently depends on the future OP-INTERFACE capability; it does not select C3. B2 seeks primary provenance or a direct permission record. B3 asks qualified counsel and a rights researcher to compare the exact source assertions. B4 retains the current media as a dated owner exception with its conflicts and missing provenance recorded.

## Decision C - global treatment of procedural covers

Measured only at runtime: the observed browser paint path samples no artwork pixels. It uses record seeds plus static repository palette and style assignments. The creation and research provenance of those assignments is undocumented, so this finding does not establish what sources informed them.

C1 retains artist-associated Pigment covers. C2 replaces them with artist-neutral Pigment covers. Under either option every applicable cover must be visibly and accessibly labelled `Pigment cover - not the artwork`. C3 applies the metadata-only capability globally to all 61 existing cover-backed records. C4 applies C3 provisionally while bounded counsel and reader-comprehension review occur, followed by owner re-decision.

C remains independent of A and B. A3 and B1 use the same presentation capability at record scope without forcing a global C3 policy.

## Decision D - jurisdiction and sequencing

I don't know which jurisdiction governs each question or whether owner, host, and reader-facing conduct differ. Candidate jurisdictions for bounded review are the owner's country and legal operating domicile, Turkey only if confirmed as relevant, United States federal law and any relevant state contact, Sweden for the af Klint materials, and specifically named target-distribution countries. Other jurisdictions remain unknown.

D1 seeks bounded counsel advice before downstream implementation. D2 permits A3 and/or B1 as record-scoped interim treatments while counsel is sought; C remains independently selected or deferred. D3 retains current behavior through A4, B4, and C1 while seeking counsel. D4 bounds counsel review to named intended jurisdictions without authorizing territorial runtime behavior.

Counsel questions remain limited to which named jurisdiction applies to each identified conduct; what the exact source-asserted CC versions require for the current presentation in that jurisdiction; whether thumbnail resizing has a relevant consequence there; how that jurisdiction treats the separately asserted media layer for the 3D and flat-work groups; what additional evidence would address the af Klint conflicts; and whether the artist-associated runtime covers raise a question independent of reproduction.

## Per-record assertion register

Before final synthesis, the six affected records must each identify the underlying work; exact media asset and source page or revision; source-asserted media author; source-asserted licence family and version; any work-level assertion; conflicting or missing assertions; residual unknowns; selected A or B treatment; metadata-only scope if selected; and candidate jurisdictions.

## Routing boundary

This revision authorizes no production edit, implementation, merge, deployment, workflow transition, or legal conclusion. It introduces no backend or PLATFORM machinery. OP-INTERFACE is a future dependency, not an authorization. The Coordinator must not resume until the recorded state/message divergence is reconciled by the appropriate protocol authority.
rationale: The challenge correctly exposes two proxies for outcomes: no-media selections currently render a procedural cover, and a literal-token count can fall when vocabulary changes. The specialist panel found that the first draft's C3 coupling would solve the renderer issue by silently turning record-scoped A and B choices into a global visual-policy choice. The smallest coherent revision defines one metadata-only reader outcome supplied later through OP-INTERFACE, permits A3 and B1 to invoke it independently at record scope, and leaves C3 as the separate global owner policy. It also narrows CH-4 to observed runtime behavior, treats contributor and licence values as source assertions, and makes future guards and reader evidence explicit requirements rather than present facts.

In final synthesis, disposition CH-1 through CH-5 against this revision and preserve the three partial defenses rather than treating every challenge statement as accepted wholesale.
Keep A3 and B1 independent of global C3; record their shared future OP-INTERFACE dependency and the precedence of record-scoped metadata-only treatment over C1/C2 for selected records.

acceptance_criteria: The owner decision record contains an explicit selection or explicit deferral for A, B, C, and D, including every accepted consequence and every OP-INTERFACE dependency.

A per-record assertion register exists for all six affected records and separately identifies the underlying work, exact media asset and source page or revision, source-asserted media author, source-asserted licence family and version, conflicting or missing assertions, residual unknowns, selected treatment, and candidate jurisdictions.

The complete six-record evidence set remains grouped analytically as three photographs of three-dimensional works, two photographs of flat works, and one unnamed or conflicted media asset governed by B. The grouping is not represented as a demonstrated legal distinction.

Statements about Sailko, Francesco Bini, and the applicable CC labels are attributed to the relevant source pages or generated source registry as source assertions, not stated as Pigment findings about authorship, authority, or legal effect.

If A1 is selected, each of the five A1-migrated records identifies its exact media asset and preserves the source-asserted author, licence family and version, source link, and matching generated visitor credit; none of those five records remains described by the `pd` token.

If A1 is selected, the legacy literal-token ratchet is retired only with future successor guards scoped to the five A1-migrated records. The sixth record is included only if Decision B separately changes it. The successor guards preserve attribution continuity, are demonstrated to be non-vacuous by recorded negative controls, and are requirements for later evidence rather than claims about the present repository.
A vocabulary migration is reported only as treatment of the token-description defect; it is not reported as resolving source authority, governing jurisdiction, or another legal question.

A3 and B1 each independently depend on a record-scoped metadata-only presentation capability supplied by a future OP-INTERFACE task. Neither selection requires C3, and this revision authorizes no interface implementation.

Metadata-only is a deliberate text presentation, never an empty frame, blank region, broken image, loading state, or error state. It preserves title, artist, date where available, navigation and links, existing record actions, and a plain media-status explanation, while rendering no image, canvas, image-role equivalent, or image alt text.

Record-scoped metadata-only treatment covers the artwork-detail page and every compact or secondary surface that would otherwise substitute an artwork image or Pigment cover, including cards, list entries, arcs, rails, and related-work surfaces.
A genuinely independent editorial cover may remain only when it is not presented as the artwork or its substitute and is visibly and accessibly labelled `Editorial cover - not the artwork`.

Decision C remains a separate global owner policy for the 61 existing cover-backed records: C1 retains artist-associated Pigment covers, C2 uses artist-neutral Pigment covers, C3 applies metadata-only globally, and C4 applies C3 provisionally pending review.

Under C1 or C2, every applicable cover is visibly and accessibly labelled `Pigment cover - not the artwork`; the artwork, any photograph or scan, the Pigment cover, and the metadata-only presentation remain distinct layers.

The C record states only that the observed current runtime paint path samples no artwork pixels. Palette and style values are described as static repository assignments whose creation and research provenance is undocumented.

Reader comprehension is evaluated separately from jurisdictional or counsel questions. Later tests, guards, accessibility review, and browser evidence support observable reader outcomes but do not substitute for them.

Any jurisdiction-specific conclusion is supplied by qualified counsel for the jurisdiction it names. Otherwise the artifact says `I don't know`, names candidate jurisdictions, identifies still-unknown jurisdictions, and states what evidence would answer the bounded question.

RIGHTS-001 introduces no backend, database, scheduled job, private asset store, human review queue, server-side policy engine, or runtime territorial evaluation. OP-INTERFACE is recorded only as a future presentation dependency, and PLATFORM remains outside scope.

The revision carries none of the five stale task-id-conflict references, does not revive GESAM, and authorizes no production edit, implementation, merge, deployment, workflow transition, or legal conclusion.
risks: The unreconciled task state may cause the Coordinator to reject or misroute a valid round-two message if it resumes from `intake`.
A future OP-INTERFACE specification could accidentally make record-scoped metadata-only treatment global, or fail to give it precedence over C1/C2 for A3/B1 records.
A metadata-only state that behaves like an empty frame, loading failure, or disabled record would satisfy a technical absence check while failing the reader outcome.
Compact and secondary surfaces may continue substituting a Pigment cover unless the record-scoped treatment follows the artwork record across all relevant surfaces.
A genuinely independent editorial cover may be mistaken for the affected artwork unless both visible and accessible labels preserve the distinction.
A future successor guard may measure another proxy, or silently include the sixth B-governed record, unless its scope and negative controls are explicit.
The 3+2+1 evidence grouping may be overstated into a legal distinction or allowed to erase per-record source and media differences.
The no-runtime-pixel-sampling finding may be overstated into a conclusion about palette and style provenance, which remains undocumented.
C3 materially reduces Pigment's visual continuity across 61 records and remains an owner decision distinct from A3 and B1.
No qualified counsel has answered the named-jurisdiction questions, so no option can be represented as a legal determination.
confidence: high: the decision architecture, current renderer fallback, literal-token guard, source-registry distinctions, task-id history, and state/message divergence are repository-grounded; low on governing jurisdiction, source authority, legal effect, palette/style creation provenance, and reader comprehension because those remain unevidenced or require bounded review
